items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1969-01-27
items.q: I played with Mud Carey's brother

ctx.x: Well, just that he told me that you went out there and, uh, you laid the hole down and never came back. He left. Right, right. Didn't get you pay or anything. Never. But anyway, uh, I wanted to ask you about, uh, that clarinet player from out of the country that quit playing. You know the man I'm talking about? Oh yeah.

I was playing with that band. After all these boys left from there, I went to play with that band. You know what I mean? Oh yeah, you're talking about, uh, well he got a French name. Lili. That's his name. That's all I know his name, Lili. He was a good boy, you know that boy was a nice, class day. And after I was down, I got him to come play with, uh, yeah, when I first came down here, I played with Mud Carey's brother, you know, and, uh, I got him to come here to, uh, Jack Carey, you know, to play down here…
He wouldn't fool the clan anymore. Was he as good as Edmund Hall?

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1959-11-08
items.q: Mud Carey came out, he used to come out, you know like on Saturdays night and play with him you see.

ctx.x: Mud Carey came out, he used to come out, you know like on Saturdays night and play with him you see. But I tell you, now Mud Carey was a fellow, was more of a Dixieland player, you see. Yeah. Well them fellows were musical. They were strictly musical, them fellows there. All them fellows were realists, you know what I mean. Yeah. And so he'd come out on Saturdays and then he would always want the fellows to play in the style he played you see. You know what I mean. More live and jazzy like, you know what I mean.…

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1964-03-21
items.q: Jack Carey, Mud Carey, he used to come out and play, too.

ctx.x: Chip, yeah, Chip. I knew Chip, too. And, uh, it's because you come out there. I don't know what you call it. What he played? I don't know what you mean. Joe Oliver. He used to come out and play with Ori bands, you see. Uh-huh. And, uh, so, so, Jack Carey, Mud Carey, he used to come out and play, too. Mm-hmm. He came out and played with this band they had in the country. The older band was there before Washington. But after the trumpet player got drowned, well, they got him to play trumpet with them.
